title: Kissed German Minari Skewers
description: A quick, yeasty German take on minari skewers, these bites are sweet, tangy, and kid-friendly.
instructions: Trim, wash, and cut 200g minari stems into 2-inch pieces.
In a bowl whisk together 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tsp grated ginger, minced garlic, 1 tsp honey, and 2 tsp rice vinegar.
Thread each minari stem onto a soaked wooden skewer, leaving a small gap between pieces.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering but not smoking.
Place the skewers in the skillet, cooking 2-3 minutes per side, turning once, until the stems are tender and slightly charred.
While the skewers are frying, toast the whole wheat bread slices on a separate pan or toaster until lightly browned.
Sprinkle 2 tbsp grated emmental cheese over the hot skewers and let melt for 30 seconds.
Drizzle the prepared sauce over the cheese-topped skewers, tossing gently to coat evenly.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then remove from heat.
Serve the hot skewers on a plate alongside the toasted bread, offering a quick, yeasty snack that kids will love.
